summary.finding: Not an accuracy measurement: 22 of these 25 prompts are only 'Show me <report title>' (agency-internal names), and several gold results are empty or truncated at 500 rows locally. The gold set needs real questions written per report (docs/18 P1.1). Of all 79: 12 real questions, 6 scorable.

cases.question: Give me the email and phone number for all users in my system.
cases.title: User emails and phone numbers
cases.sql: SELECT u.first_name AS `First name`, u.last_name AS `Last name`, u.user_type AS `User type`, u.email AS `Email`, c.phone_number AS `Phone number` FROM `user` u LEFT JOIN contact c ON c.contact_id = u.contact_id ORDER BY u.last_name, u.first_name
assumptions: 'Users' means the user accounts (donors, surrogates, intended parents, sperm donors, IP reps), not staff/admin accounts.
Email is the one on the user's own account.
Phone number comes from the user's linked contact record, since accounts don't store a phone; it is blank when the contact has none (about 60% of contacts).
All accounts are included, active or not.

cases.question: Show me NP User.
cases.title: NP Users
cases.sql: SELECT np_user_id AS "NP User ID", first_name AS "First Name", last_name AS "Last Name", email AS "Email", phone AS "Phone", user_type AS "User Type", date_of_birth AS "Date of Birth", active AS "Active", created AS "Created", last_login AS "Last Login" FROM user_np ORDER BY last_name, first_name
assumptions: 'NP User' is read as the list of NP user accounts (all 80), not a count or a specific person.
Showing basic identity, contact, type and activity details; password information is excluded.
No filters applied, including active status, since all users are currently active.

cases.question: Show me Hellosigns (IP).
cases.title: Hellosigns (IP) – e-signature requests sent to intended parents
cases.sql: select h.hellosign_id as 'Request #', h.signature_request_id as 'Signature Request ID', h.created as 'Created', h.completed as 'Completed', concat(a.first_name,' ',a.last_name) as 'Created By', concat(u.first_name,' ',u.last_name) as 'Intended Parent (Recipient)', cr.status as 'Recipient Status' from hellosign h join contract_rel cr on cr.parent_id=h.hellosign_id and cr.user_type='user' join user u on u.user_id=cr.user_id left join admin a on a.admin_id=h.created_by_id where u.user_type='IP' order by h.created desc
assumptions: 'Hellosigns (IP)' means e-signature requests where at least one recipient is an intended-parent (IP) user, mirroring the existing 'Hellosigns (GC/ED)' report for surrogates/donors.
IP rep users and non-platform/admin recipients are excluded.
A request with several IP recipients appears once per recipient.
Recipient status is that recipient's own signing status (sent, viewed, signed, undelivered), separate from the request's overall completed date.

cases.question: Show me Hellosigns (GC/ED).
cases.title: Hellosigns (GC/ED) – signature requests
cases.sql:
select h.hellosign_id as `Request #`, h.signature_request_id as `Signature Request`, h.created as `Created`, h.completed as `Completed`, concat(a.first_name,' ',a.last_name) as `Created By`,
 count(r.relationship_id) as `Signers`, coalesce(sum(r.status='signed'),0) as `Signed`, coalesce(sum(r.status='sent'),0) as `Sent`, coalesce(sum(r.status='viewed'),0) as `Viewed`, coalesce(sum(r.status='undelivered'),0) as `Undelivered`
from hellosign h left join admin a on a.admin_id=h.created_by_id left join contract_rel r on r.parent_id=h.hellosign_id
group by h.hellosign_id, h.signature_request_id, h.created, h.completed, a.first_name, a.last_name order by h.created desc
assumptions: 'Hellosigns (GC/ED)' is the name of a saved report, but its stored definition is unusable, so I rebuilt it as a list of all e-signature requests.
Each row is one signature request, with the admin who created it and a count of its signers by status (signed, sent, viewed, undelivered).
I did not split requests into GC versus ED, because the data has no direct link between a request and a case type.
A blank completed date means the request has not been completed.
Sorted newest first.

cases.question: Show me Campaigns (IP).
cases.title: Campaigns (IP)
cases.sql:
SELECT c.campaign_id AS `Campaign ID`, c.internal_title AS `Campaign`, CASE WHEN c.active=1 THEN 'Active' ELSE 'Inactive' END AS `Status`, c.stage AS `Stage`, c.start_trigger AS `Start trigger`, c.start_trigger_val AS `Start trigger value`, c.day_trigger AS `Timing value`, c.start_mode AS `Timing unit`, c.end_trigger AS `End trigger`, c.end_trigger_val AS `End trigger value`,
(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM campaign_flow f WHERE f.campaign_id=c.campaign_id) AS `Flow steps`,
(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_campaign cc WHERE cc.campaign_id=c.campaign_id) AS `Cases enrolled`
FROM campaign c WHERE c.case_type='ip'
ORDER BY c.campaign_id
assumptions: 'Campaigns (IP)' means the campaign definitions set up for intended-parent (IP) cases.
Both active and inactive campaigns are included, with status shown.
Flow steps and cases enrolled are counts per campaign.

cases.question: Show me Campaigns (GC/ED).
cases.title: Campaigns (GC/ED)
cases.sql: select c.campaign_id as 'Campaign ID', c.internal_title as 'Campaign', upper(c.case_type) as 'Case Type', case when c.active=1 then 'Active' else 'Inactive' end as 'Campaign Status', c.start_trigger as 'Starts On', c.day_trigger as 'Timing Value', c.start_mode as 'Timing Unit', c.end_trigger as 'Ends On', count(cc.case_campaign_id) as 'Cases Enrolled', coalesce(sum(cc.flow_status in ('starting','flowing','waiting')),0) as 'In Progress', coalesce(sum(cc.flow_status like 'finished%'),0) as 'Finished', coalesce(sum(cc.flow_status='stopped'),0) as 'Stopped' from campaign c left join case_campaign cc on cc.campaign_id=c.campaign_id where c.case_type in ('gc','ed') group by c.campaign_id, c.internal_title, c.case_type, c.active, c.start_trigger, c.day_trigger, c.start_mode, c.end_trigger order by c.case_type, c.campaign_id
assumptions: 'Campaigns (GC/ED)' is read as the marketing/communication campaigns set up for gestational carrier (GC) and egg donor (ED) cases.
The saved report definition with that name contains no usable query, so I built the report from the campaign setup and case enrollment data.
Each row is one campaign with counts of cases enrolled in it.
In progress means starting, flowing or waiting; finished includes those ended by a trigger; stopped is shown separately; enrollments with no status are only counted in the total.

cases.question: Show me GC/ED Confirmed Email & Last Login.
cases.title: GC/ED Confirmed Email & Last Login
cases.sql: SELECT u.first_name AS "First Name", u.last_name AS "Last Name", CASE u.user_type WHEN 'surrogate' THEN 'GC' ELSE 'ED' END AS "Type", u.email AS "Email", u.last_login AS "Last Login" FROM user u WHERE u.user_type IN ('surrogate','donor') AND u.confirmed_email = 1 ORDER BY u.last_login DESC
assumptions: GC means users of type surrogate (gestational carriers); ED means users of type donor (egg donors). Sperm donors and intended parents are excluded.
Only users who have confirmed their email address are listed.
Last login is shown as stored; users who have never logged in show it blank and appear last.
Inactive accounts are not excluded.

cases.question: Show me All Users.
cases.title: All Users
cases.sql: SELECT user_id AS `User ID`, first_name AS `First Name`, last_name AS `Last Name`, email AS `Email`, user_type AS `User Type`, CASE WHEN active = 1 THEN 'Active' ELSE 'Inactive' END AS `Status`, created AS `Created`, last_login AS `Last Login` FROM `user` ORDER BY last_name, first_name
assumptions: 'All Users' means every user account in the system, regardless of type or whether it is active.
Showing name, email, user type, active/inactive status, creation date and last login; users who never logged in have an empty last login.
Sorted by last name, then first name.

cases.question: Show me Another NP User lookup.
cases.title: Saved report "Another NP User lookup"
cases.sql: SELECT custom_report_id AS `Report ID`, report_title AS `Report title`, active AS `Active (1=yes)`, widget AS `Dashboard widget (1=yes)`, warning AS `Has warning (1=yes)`, created AS `Created`, date_depricated AS `Deprecated on`, hyperlink AS `Link`, report_headers AS `Report headers`, report_query AS `Report query` FROM custom_report WHERE report_title = 'Another NP User lookup' ORDER BY created
assumptions: Read 'Another NP User lookup' as the title of a saved custom report, so this shows the report's definition rather than a list of NP users.
Two saved reports have this title: one active and one deprecated. Both are shown.
The stored headers and query text for these reports are placeholder-like text, so they can't be run as a real report.

cases.question: Show me IP Workflow.Snippet.
cases.title: IP Workflow.Snippet custom reports
cases.sql: SELECT custom_report_id AS `Report ID`, report_title AS `Report title`, CASE WHEN active = 1 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS `Active`, CASE WHEN widget = 1 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS `Dashboard widget`, created AS `Created`, date_depricated AS `Deprecated on`, hyperlink AS `Hyperlink`, report_headers AS `Report headers` FROM custom_report WHERE report_title = 'IP Workflow.Snippet' ORDER BY created
assumptions: 'IP Workflow.Snippet' is read as the title of a saved custom report, so this lists the report definitions with that title (there are 4).
The reports' stored query text is not run or shown; only descriptive details such as status, creation and deprecation dates are listed.
Deprecated reports are included, with their deprecation date shown.

cases.question: Show me IP Snippet.Workflow.
cases.title: IP Snippet.Workflow – saved report definition
cases.sql: SELECT custom_report_id AS `Report ID`, report_title AS `Report title`, CASE WHEN active = 1 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS `Active`, CASE WHEN widget = 1 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS `Shown as dashboard widget`, CASE WHEN warning = 1 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS `Has warning`, created AS `Created`, date_depricated AS `Deprecated on`, hyperlink AS `Hyperlink`, report_headers AS `Report headers` FROM custom_report WHERE report_title = 'IP Snippet.Workflow'
assumptions: 'IP Snippet.Workflow' is read as the name of a saved custom report, not a request for case data. Exactly one report has that title.
The result shows the report's details (status, creation date, headers). It does not run the report's own stored query, because that text isn't a usable query.
I did not look up IP cases or to-do snippets. Tell me if that's what you meant.

cases.question: Show me General Form Submission.
cases.title: General Form Submissions
cases.sql:
SELECT g.general_form_submission_id AS `Submission ID`, g.form_id AS `Form ID`, f.display_title AS `Form Title`, f.backend_title AS `Internal Form Title`, f.form_type AS `Form Type`, g.created AS `Submitted At`, g.browser AS `Browser`, CASE WHEN g.has_files = 1 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS `Has Files`
FROM general_form_submission g
LEFT JOIN form f ON f.form_id = g.form_id
ORDER BY g.general_form_submission_id
assumptions: Showing every general form submission, one row per submission, with the title and type of the form it belongs to.
The raw submitted form content is left out because it is long and unreadable; it can be added if needed.
The submitting contact is left out because it is empty for all submissions.
Every submission has the same recorded time, so the list is ordered by submission number.

questions.question: Which cycle data do you want in the cycle report?
What would you like to see under "IP SSN"?
options: The saved report definition named "IP SSN" (title, status, created date) – its stored query text is not usable
A list of intended-parent contacts showing whether an SSN is on file (yes/no; the number itself is protected and cannot be shown)
The "SSN + Relationship" / "Just SSN" forms and their submission status for intended-parent cases

questions.question: Which "calculator" do you want to see?
options: The custom report called "Case Calculator" (its definition and status)
The baby growth calculator's custom responses (agency-specific labels, images and texts)

cases.question: Show me Case Calculator.
cases.title: Case Calculator report definition
cases.sql: SELECT custom_report_id AS "Report ID", report_title AS "Report title", active AS "Active (1=yes)", widget AS "Dashboard widget (1=yes)", date_depricated AS "Date deprecated", created AS "Created", report_headers AS "Report headers", report_query AS "Report query text" FROM custom_report WHERE report_title = 'Case Calculator'
assumptions: 'Case Calculator' is read as the saved custom report with that exact title, not as a data calculation.
There is only one such report, and its stored query text is placeholder-like prose, so it can't be run as a real report.
The report is flagged active but has a deprecation date of 2026-08-06.

cases.question: Show me GC Monitoring.
cases.title: GC Monitoring – lab/monitoring records for gestational carriers
cases.sql:
SELECT g.case_file_name AS `GC Case`, g.case_type AS `Case Type`, g.stage AS `Stage`, e.event_name AS `Monitoring Event`, l.date_labs_drawn AS `Labs Drawn`, l.time_labs_drawn AS `Time Drawn`, l.clinic_name AS `Clinic`, l.result AS `Result`, l.notes AS `Notes`, a.first_name AS `Created By (First Name)`, a.last_name AS `Created By (Last Name)`
FROM lab l
JOIN gc_case g ON g.case_id = l.gc_case_id
JOIN event e ON e.event_id = l.event_id
LEFT JOIN admin a ON a.admin_id = l.created_by_id
ORDER BY l.date_labs_drawn DESC
assumptions: 'GC Monitoring' is interpreted as the monitoring (lab draw) records recorded against gestational carrier cases, newest first.
The saved report called 'GC Monitoring' has no usable definition (its text is placeholder content), so I built this from the lab records instead.
Only lab records linked to a gestational carrier case are included; those linked only to intended parents or egg donor cases are excluded.
Monitoring event is the lab event type (e.g. Beta, Ultrasound, HCG, FDA).

cases.question: Show me Sperm Donor Matches.
cases.title: Sperm Donor Matches
cases.sql: select mq.matching_queue_id as `Match ID`, ip.case_file_name as `Intended Parent`, sd.case_file_name as `Sperm Donor`, mq.status as `Match Status`, mq.donation_type as `Donation Type`, mq.created as `Created`, mq.ip_sent_date as `Sent to IP`, mq.match_accepted as `Match Accepted`, mq.match_break as `Match Broken` from matching_queue mq join ip_case ip on ip.case_id = mq.case_id join gc_case sd on sd.case_id = mq.gc_case_id where mq.matching_type = 'sperm_donor' order by mq.created desc
assumptions: 'Sperm Donor Matches' means every sperm donor match entry in the matching queue, pairing an intended parent with a sperm donor.
All statuses are included (matched, broken, archived, sent, and so on). The status is shown so you can filter it.
Newest entries are listed first.
A saved custom report with this name exists, but its definition is placeholder text and not usable, so I built the report from the matching data.

cases.question: Show me GC Average Days in Screening Sample report.

questions.question: The saved "GC Average Days in Screening Sample" report has no usable definition (its text is placeholder filler), and the database does not record the date a case entered screening. How should I calculate days in screening?
options: Average days from today back to the earliest completed screening step, for cases currently in the screening stage
Average days between the earliest and latest completed screening steps per case
Just list the cases currently in screening with their screening steps completed (no average)

questions.question: Which cases count as GCs?
options: Surrogates, egg donors and sperm donors (all cases)

cases.question: Show me IP Average Days in Matching sample.
cases.title: IP Average Days in Matching
cases.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS `Matching Entries Counted`, COUNT(DISTINCT ip_case_id) AS `IP Cases`, ROUND(AVG(DATEDIFF(match_fully_approved, move_to_matching)), 1) AS `Average Days in Matching`, MIN(DATEDIFF(match_fully_approved, move_to_matching)) AS `Shortest (Days)`, MAX(DATEDIFF(match_fully_approved, move_to_matching)) AS `Longest (Days)` FROM matching_days_report WHERE move_to_matching IS NOT NULL AND match_fully_approved IS NOT NULL AND match_fully_approved >= move_to_matching
assumptions: Days in matching = days from when the IP case moved into matching to when the match was fully approved.
Only entries with both dates are counted; entries still waiting on either date are left out.
Entries where the approval date is earlier than the move-to-matching date look like data errors and are excluded.
Each entry is counted separately, so a case with more than one entry counts more than once in the average.
I read 'sample' as part of the report's name, not as a request for a data sample.

cases.question: Show me Egg Donor Matches.
cases.title: Egg Donor Matches
cases.sql: SELECT mq.matching_queue_id AS `Queue Entry`, ip.case_file_name AS `Intended Parent Case`, ed.case_file_name AS `Egg Donor Case`, mq.status AS `Match Status`, mq.donation_type AS `Donation Type`, mq.created AS `Queued On`, mq.ip_sent_date AS `Sent to IP`, mq.match_accepted AS `Match Accepted`, mq.match_break AS `Match Broken`, mq.active AS `Active` FROM matching_queue mq JOIN ip_case ip ON ip.case_id = mq.case_id JOIN gc_case ed ON ed.case_id = mq.gc_case_id WHERE mq.matching_type = 'donor' ORDER BY mq.created DESC
assumptions: 'Egg Donor Matches' means every pairing of an intended-parent case with an egg donor case in the matching queue.
All statuses are included (matched, broken, archived, queued, etc.); the status column lets you filter to actual matches.
The saved report named 'Egg Donor Matches' contains no usable definition, so the report was built from the matching queue data.
Newest entries are listed first.

cases.question: Show me Test matchsheet mapping.
cases.title: Test match sheet header – question mapping
cases.sql: SELECT t.title AS match_sheet_template, h.section_name AS section, h.header_name AS header, h.active AS header_active, q.question_order AS question_order, q.question_text AS question, q.question_type AS question_type, q.active AS question_active, q.mapped_table AS mapped_table, q.mapped_column AS mapped_column, fq.form_question_id AS mapped_form_question_id FROM match_sheet_header h JOIN match_sheet_template t ON t.match_sheet_id = h.match_sheet_id LEFT JOIN match_sheet_question q ON q.header_id = h.header_id LEFT JOIN form_question fq ON fq.form_question_id = q.mapped_form_question_id WHERE h.header_name = 'Test' ORDER BY t.title, h.section_order, h.header_order, q.question_order
assumptions: 'Test matchsheet mapping' is read as the mapping of questions under match sheet headers named 'Test' (4 headers across several templates).
Mapping means the target table and column each question fills, plus any linked form question.
Both active and inactive headers and questions are shown, with their active flags, so you can filter them.
Questions with no mapping are included, with blank mapping columns.

cases.question: Show me ED Matchsheet Mapping.
cases.title: ED Match Sheet Mapping (questions mapped to data fields)
cases.sql: select t.title as "Match Sheet", case when t.active = 1 then 'Active' else 'Inactive' end as "Sheet Status", h.section_name as "Section", h.header_name as "Header", q.question_order as "Question Order", q.question_text as "Question", q.question_type as "Input Type", q.mapped_table as "Mapped To (Record Type)", q.mapped_column as "Mapped To (Field)", q.mapped_form_question_id as "Mapped Form Question ID", case when q.active = 1 then 'Active' else 'Inactive' end as "Question Status" from match_sheet_template t join match_sheet_header h on h.match_sheet_id = t.match_sheet_id join match_sheet_question q on q.header_id = h.header_id where (t.title like '%ED Match Sheet%' or t.title like '%IP/ED%') and (q.mapped_table is not null or q.mapped_column is not null or q.mapped_form_question_id is not null) order by t.match_sheet_id, h.section_order, h.header_order, q.question_order
assumptions: Read 'ED Matchsheet Mapping' as the match sheet questions that are mapped to a record type, field or intake form question, rather than the separate 'ED - Mapping' intake form.
Included every match sheet whose name refers to ED: 'ED Match Sheet', 'Copy 1 ED Match Sheet' and '(DEFAULT) Escrow Match Sheet IP/ED'.
Included both active and inactive sheets and questions, and labelled their status.
Showed only questions that have at least one mapping; unmapped questions are left out.

cases.question: Show me Status.
cases.title: Status list
cases.sql: SELECT status AS `Status`, stage AS `Stage`, contact_type AS `Contact type`, active AS `Active` FROM status ORDER BY stage, contact_type, status
assumptions: Interpreted 'Status' as the list of workflow statuses defined in the system, not a count of cases or contacts per status.
Showing every status with its stage and contact type; all are active.
